chapter: Boyhood in Evergreen and Calhoun school
title: Jerry Martin and the Silas Green and Rabbit's Foot minstrel shows
summary: As a child he watched visiting minstrel shows and parades; trombonist Jerry Martin, a neighbour, encouraged him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well, at this point -- when you were playing trumpet, did you play anywhere except in this band, or was that the extent of your playing?

That was the extent of my playing, with the exception, I had -- I got a couple of nights work that really cut wherever they knocked me up. The first time I had ever played in the band -- in fact there lived next door to me a lady who was married to one of the finest trombone players ever.
I can't recall his name -- Martin -- Jerry Martin. He was with the Silas Green shows. Did you ever hear of that?
Yeah, uh-huh. Well, all the minstrels

used to come in, naturally, come into to town, and when we -- I used to -- four or five years I used to sit and watch. They couldn't get me away because that music -- I don't know. It meant so much to me. And my father would take me by the hand and go -- let me go and hear until it got too -- kind of late. And he'd bring me home, and he'd go back out.

Now Jerry Martin, he was friends with a lady lived next door. They were very good friends. And I used to hear him play, and I talked with him, and he encouraged me to keep studying, whatnot, and the parades, you know how they used to parade through the street with the red coats on and shiny instruments, and this, and this is the trombone. Oh, man, that was it! And that was about -- let's see -- Rabbit's Foot Minstrel, all of them.
Was Rabbit's Foot Ma Rainey's show?
